dedupe_keys.name: supplier supply chain disruptions survey rethink gsc austria denmark germany hungary

description: The Supply Chain Disruptions Survey asked medium-sized and large manufacturing firms in Austria, Denmark, Germany and Hungary about their recent experiences and expectations with suppliers, between mid-2023 and spring 2024. Questions cover input-output links with suppliers, the role of intangible assets and services alongside physical inputs, and how firms reacted to shocks in global supply chains. It was run in the EU-funded project RETHINK-GSC (Rethinking Global Supply Chains: Measurement, Impact and Policy) by Márta Bisztray, Gábor Békés, Alexandros Charos, Klaus Friesenbichler, Miklós Koren, Balázs Lengyel, Birgit Meyer and colleagues. The aggregated first round was published in 2024 and updated in March 2025 with extra spring 2024 responses, mostly from Germany, under the Open Data Commons Attribution licence as a tar archive of about 533 KB on RADAR. A further deposit of October 2025 (about 663 KB) is under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 but carries no description. Access is free. Caveats: the public files are aggregated, the sample covers four European countries and mostly manufacturing, and response counts are not stated on the pages read. For simulation it gives firm-reported frequencies of supplier disruptions and responses, useful to calibrate firm behaviour in supply chain disruption and recovery models. Related catalogue records include the SCDisrupt synthetic benchmark and the Eora2 global supply chain database.
